passages.note: Bill overview lists Griffin as prime sponsor; the Governor signed the bill into law.
House Final Reading shows the bill passed 39-16-5-0-0 with Griffin voting Y.

passages.provision_quote: Supports policies that establish new customer classes, rate designs and cost allocation formulas for extra high load factor customers that are reasonable and necessary to prevent cost shifts to residential customers from extra high load factor customers.
passages.note: The enacted text creates reporting and commission-optional rate/cost-allocation mechanisms for high load factor customers, aimed at preventing cost shifts to residential ratepayers, but sets no moratorium, no absolute cost-pass-through bar, no impact-assessment or community-benefit approval gate, and no permitting streamlining.

rows.reasoning: HB2756 (2026), which Griffin prime-sponsored and voted for and which the Governor signed, requires periodic reporting on new extra high load factor customer interconnections and lets the corporation commission or a public power entity's governing body optionally set billing/cost-allocation terms 'necessary to prevent cost shifts to residential customers from extra high load factor customers.' That shows a direction toward protecting residential ratepayers and reporting demand, but it does not impose a moratorium, does not bar utilities from passing costs to residential customers outright, does not require impact assessments or community benefit requirements before approval, and does not touch permitting speed, so it cannot separate rungs 1 through 4.
